decisions.quote: We begin by replicating the LCAPM tests of AP using their original methodology, which is based on GMM and uses portfolios as test assets. We cover their original time period of 1962 to 1999 and a more recent period 2000 to 2015.
decisions.reason: In addition to reconstructing and re-analysing the original 1962-1999 NYSE/AMEX sample from CRSP and Compustat, the paper re-tests Acharya and Pedersen's (2005) LCAPM predictions on new samples and time periods (2000-2015 and 1926-1961 NYSE/AMEX stocks, as well as 1973-1999 and 2000-2015 NASDAQ stocks). Under the codebook, using new data or a different sample to re-test a previously published finding qualifies as a replication, so the shipped type 'replication' is correct.

decisions.quote: In the large majority of cases, our replication evidence fails to support that the main LCAPM predictions all hold simultaneously. Next, we extend tests of the LCAPM following the Lee (2011) methodology and expanding to: (1) three different time periods spanning 90 years, (2) add NASDAQ stocks, (3) use four alternative liquidity measures, and (4) add risk or characteristic factors. Our extension evidence always fails to support that the main predictions of the Lee two-beta LCAPM and of the four-beta LCAPM hold at the same time. Overall, we fail to support that liquidity risk matters in the specific functional form predicted by the LCAPM.
decisions.reason: With type resolved as 'replication', the authors state an explicit overall verdict that both their replication tests (failing to replicate the second-stage cross-sectional tests and failing to support that the main LCAPM predictions hold simultaneously in the large majority of cases) and their extension tests fail to support the LCAPM predictions. Under Rule 1 of the codebook, the authors' overall verdict decides the outcome as 'failed'.
